brief:
Associates of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have indicated openness to forming a unity government that excludes National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir's party, according to Middle East Eye. The message was conveyed to Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party team, suggesting potential flexibility in coalition negotiations.

The development signals possible reconfiguration of Israel's governing coalition, though details on broader negotiations and the status of other coalition partners remain unclear.
dek: Report: Netanyahu's allies open to unity government without Ben Gvir’s party Associates of Benjamin Netanyahu have told Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot’s team they would accept a unity government without National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir's party,…
title: Netanyahu allies signal willingness to form government without Ben Gvir
